checks.finding: tasks.md T-001–T-009 identify externally visible contracts, execution evidence, protected launch or untrusted notification surfaces and use high/tdd. T-010 confines medium/acceptance-first work to controlled evaluation and reviewed adoption references, excluding capability and authorization algorithms. Amended T-011 Risk/Risk Rationale explicitly classify runtime omission selection and setup/schema parsing as high/tdd. Data Migration: None and Breaking API: No are accompanied by compatibility and rollback requirements; no safety, regulated or irreversible destructive surface requires critical classification.

tasks.md T-011, Readiness bugfix diagnostic path and Done When (lines 585–598), requires tests-first Red/Green and retained diagnostic records but does not require evidence that the failing tests were committed before implementation or a named independent reviewer verdict for the newly high-risk correction. The generic independent quality verification at line 9 and quality-gate acceptance at line 597 do not specify those evidence requirements; design.md Test Strategy requires pre-implementation Red but likewise does not require the test commit or named verdict. T-001–T-009 explicitly require both in their Done When sections. Consequently the amended T-011 completion criteria can be satisfied without the inspectable chronology and attributable independent review required by this Critical check. Require preservation/linkage of those records without backdating history; this finding does not assert that the actual implementation lacks them.

tasks.md Shared file ordering and individual Goals separate planning, aggregation, wiring, discovery, identity, selection, transport, installed entries, maintenance and adoption into coherent contract boundaries. T-011 adds a bounded four-file readiness correction directly supporting its existing TEST-017 rollout obligation; its scope excludes unrelated algorithm changes and keeps final release dependent on adoption. The changed text does not introduce an independent oversized implementation area or artificial task fragmentation.

tasks.md functional Done When sections and acceptance-tests.md enumerate invalid revision/input, missing/duplicate/wrong-native evidence, cancelled/skipped execution, cache corruption, stale/partial discovery, identity mismatch, precedence, unsupported hosts and notification failures. T-011 diagnostic path explicitly retains mandatory behavior for unknown predicates, missing matrix values and unrecognized raw commands, and requires old-parser/new-setup typed rejection rather than a falsely claimed fallback. Frontend graphical testing is justifiably inapplicable per frontend-spec.md.

tasks.md Test Ownership maps each TEST to its AC and final owner. Core planner/selector/schema work uses unit and integration fixtures; protected transport and installed entries require integration/native entry evidence; T-010 requires actual controlled behavior comparisons. T-011 links four focused planner regressions and the prior 50-test suite to readiness, while Done When separately retains actual hosted TEST-016/017, full parity, category comparisons and exact-commit release validation. acceptance-tests.md Verification Scope expressly prevents local fixtures or dry enumeration from satisfying hosted execution.

tasks.md Shared file ordering and rollback requires task-owned restoration in a disposable checkout, before/after hashes and baseline reruns, preserving identity ledgers and frozen history. Every task has an explicit tested rollback completion criterion. T-011 additionally requires exact subset rollback in its readiness diagnostic path. infra-spec.md Rollback specifies force-full recovery for CI and a validated explicit pin/new attempt for models without weakening identity or consent checks.

tasks.md Shared file ordering assigns ownership of shared catalog/helper changes and mandates serial execution. T-004–T-007 limit shared model-policy.py changes to distinct discovery, binding, selection and launch functions; T-008 consumes transport contracts. T-011 Planned Files and Scope explicitly bound its later planner/catalog/schema repair to omission readiness, following completed predecessor ownership, while final adoption/release remains separate. No concurrent uncoordinated ownership is authorized.

tasks.md dependency explanation and Blockers describe the producer-to-consumer sequence T-001→T-008, T-009 consuming policy T-006, T-010 consuming installed entries T-008, and T-011 joining maintenance/adoption. The amended T-011 Scope explicitly permits its bounded CI readiness continuation independently of T-010 execution but preserves T-010 as a final rollout/release blocker. That distinction is supported by the readiness repair consuming CI planner artifacts rather than model trial outputs; no missing dependency or unsupported overlap is introduced.

tasks.md T-011 Readiness bugfix diagnostic path (lines 585–589) specifies the original symptom: readme-contract selects all 443 of 443 obligations and omits nothing. It requires reproduction against retained before-source bytes with command, hashes and observed-versus-expected output; investigation of condition_value handling of generated ci-plan predicates and the undeclared exact CLI setup command before selecting a correction; and four focused regression cases plus prior50/new4 Green, source-consumer proof and rollback. Unknown-condition, missing-matrix, raw-command and old-parser/new-setup controls distinguish the causal boundary. This is sufficient planned diagnostic and regression evidence; it does not establish completed hosted TEST-017.

findings.finding: tasks.md T-011 Readiness bugfix diagnostic path and Done When (lines 585–598) do not require evidence that failing tests were committed before implementation or a named independent reviewer verdict for the amended high/tdd runtime-selection correction. Generic independent quality verification (line 9), tests-first Red/Green wording (line 589), and quality-gate acceptance (line 597) leave those required records unspecified; design.md Test Strategy supplies no missing commit or named-review requirement. This permits completion without the inspectable chronology and attributable review required by HIGH-CRITICAL-EVIDENCE, whose severity is Critical. Add explicit completion requirements to preserve/link the real tests-first commit chronology and named independent verdict, without backdating or replacing retained evidence. This is a task-plan evidence gap, not a claim that implementation evidence is absent.
